newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian gilts show unusually active on bourse.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian gilts show unusually active on bourse.

text.p: Rarely traded Nigerian gilts were active on Tuesday with one trader doing three deals worth 64.5 million naira in government development stocks.
Traders speculated the prospect of lower bank interest rates coupled with the relative security of gilts over equities could have encouraged an institutional investor to enter the market.
Most participants in the sector are institutional investors, who are statutorily obliged to include the securities in their portfolios.
Traders have complained returns on government stocks were too low to attract investors. The highest rate is 12.5 percent, paid half-yearly.
"The exchange is worried that gilts and industrial loans are rarely active in our market," Hayford Alile, chief executive of the exchange, told traders on Tuesday.
He said a committee had been set up to examine why trading in the sector is low and recommend ways to reactivate it.
